hero.eyebrow: Emergency medical profiles for Sri Lankan families
hero.title: If something happens to them, a stranger should know exactly what to do.
hero.subtitle: helf gives your family a QR code — on a wallet card, a sticker, a lock-screen wallpaper — that shows a stranger only the medical details you choose, with one tap to call your contacts or 1990.
hero.trustLine: No app to install. No password to remember — just your phone number.

how.title: Setup takes less than 3 minutes
how.subtitle: Zero complicated medical jargon. Just clear, lifesaving guidance.
how.step1Body: Verify your Sri Lankan mobile number (+94) with a single OTP code. No complex passwords or email verification required.
how.step2Body: Input allergies, chronic conditions, primary doctor, and 1–3 trusted family contacts who should be called first.
how.step3Body: Save the QR wallpaper directly to your lock screen, or order a physical waterproof PVC wallet card delivered anywhere in Sri Lanka.

privacyDemo.footnote: This is the same live preview your family sees while editing a real profile — never a guess, never out of date.

features.title: Built for real situations in Sri Lanka

sharing.title: Share the responsibility
sharing.body: Invite a sibling, spouse, or caregiver to help keep a profile current — no shared logins, no single point of failure.

lostPerson.title: Lost-person mode
lostPerson.body: For dementia and memory conditions: shows a general area to help someone get home safely, never a precise address.

localMeds.title: Local medicine terms
localMeds.body: Prescription, over-the-counter, and herbal/Ayurvedic medicines are all supported — because that's what Sri Lankan medicine cabinets actually look like.

languages.title: Sinhala, Tamil, English
languages.body: The whole app and the public scan page work in all three — switch anytime, for you or for whoever scans the code.

alerts.title: You're notified when scanned
alerts.body: The moment someone scans the code, your family gets an alert by SMS and email — so you know your person was found.

revoke.title: Revoke anytime
revoke.body: Lost the card? Revoke it instantly. The old code stops working immediately — the 1990 button still works, nothing else does.

pricing.heading: Always free to create. Inexpensive to print.
pricing.subtitle: Pay in Sri Lankan Rupees (LKR) with local cards or Cash on Delivery, or in USD if you're supporting family from abroad.

groups.title: For elder care homes, insurers & employers
groups.body: Bulk enrollments with custom hospital integration and special corporate group rates.

faq.title: Questions families ask
faq.heading: Still have questions? Here's what families usually ask us.

q1.q: Is my family's medical information safe?
q1.a: Yes. Nothing is public by default. You choose exactly which fields are visible on the scan page, field by field — medicines, for example, stay private unless you turn them on.

q2.q: What exactly does a stranger see when they scan the code?
q2.a: Only the fields you've switched on — never your home address, never anything you haven't explicitly chosen to share. You can preview exactly what a stranger would see, any time.

q3.q: What if I lose the card, or it ends up with the wrong person?
q3.a: Revoke that QR code instantly from your account. It stops working immediately and shows a safe message instead, while the 1990 ambulance button still works. Then print a new one.

q4.a: Creating a profile and generating your QR code is free — no subscription needed to use the core service.

q5.q: Do I need to install an app?
q5.a: No. Managing a profile and the public scan page both work in any phone's browser — nothing to download, nothing to update.

q6.q: Can more than one family member help manage a profile?
q6.a: Yes. Invite a sibling, spouse, or caregiver with a one-time code — they can help keep information current without sharing a login.

footer.tagline: Emergency medical profiles for Sri Lankan families — in Sinhala, Tamil, and English.
footer.emergencyBody: Sri Lanka's ambulance service — available nationwide, 24/7.
footer.disclaimer: helf is not a substitute for emergency medical services. In an emergency, always call 1990 (ambulance) first.
